title: Canonical ind-etale coordinate ring of a geometric strict-local base
statement: Let s:Spec Omega to S be a geometric point of a scheme S [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-geometric-point], A=S_(s) its strict henselization [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], K any field, and u:Spec K to A. Put t=(A to S)u, E=A times_S Spec K, and a:E to Spec K [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then the canonical ring map K to Gamma(E,O_E), obtained by composing the inverse Gamma-Spec identification with a on top sections, is ind-etale, meaning a filtered colimit of etale algebras [sk-def-pe-morphisms].

source.place: Corrected Tag 0EZV proof, step 1; Tag 04HX, ind-etale affine-chart presentation and base change

proof.text: Choose an affine chart Spec R to S at the closed point. Strict-henselization residue functoriality supplies the local ring and closed-point equation. As in the affine-base proof, the structural map factors through this chart, as b:Spec A to Spec R. Apply the affine-chart ind-etale theorem to rho=Spec.preimage b and the identity identification of Spec A with the strict henselization. Cancel the monomorphic chart inclusion to regard the requested fibre product as a fibre product over Spec R. Mathlib isPushout_appTop_of_isPullback gives the ring pushout on top sections, because both factors and the chart are affine. Naturality of Gamma-Spec identifies b.appTop with rho conjugated by the canonical isomorphisms. Ind-etale maps are stable under isomorphisms and cobase change, so the other map into the ring pushout is ind-etale. Precompose by the canonical K to Gamma(Spec K) isomorphism; this is exactly the stated coordinate-ring map.

lean.statement:
theorem strictLocalBase_indEtale {S : Scheme.{u}} {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω]
    (s : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ S) (K : Type u) [Field K]
    (u : Spec (.of K) ⟶ Scheme.strictHenselizationScheme s) :
    ((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of K)).inv ≫
      (pullback.snd (Scheme.strictHenselizationStructuralMap s)
        (u ≫ Scheme.strictHenselizationStructuralMap s)).appTop).hom.IndEtale
